newsitem.title: USA: Judge rules prostitution illegal in Florida.
newsitem.headline: Judge rules prostitution illegal in Florida.

text.p: A federal judge has denied a request to legalize prostitution in Florida, saying prostitution would have a much more harmful effect on marriages than adultery, the Miami Herald reported Wednesday.
The ruling, issued March 10 but publicized only recently, came in a lawsuit filed in 1994 by a woman known as "Jane Roe," against Florida Attorney General Robert Butterworth.
Roe, a West Palm Beach woman who said she was a former call girl, had argued that if it was legal for a woman to have an abortion, she should be able to legally sell her body for sex.
In his 39-page decision, U.S. District Judge Jose Gonzalez said he did not have the power to substantively change public policy that did not affect a fundamental right.

He also said it was reasonable for prostitution to be illegal beause, "It is unquestionable that a spouse's relationship with a prostitute would have a disastrous effect on most marriages, and it is reasonable for the Legislature to conclude that such an affair would lead to greater marital strife than mere adultery."

Elliot Shaw, an attorney from West Palm Beach who represented Roe, told the newspaper that Gonzalez's ruling was "a sexist opinion. It's a constitutional slap in the face to every American man, woman and child." An appeal has already been filed with the 11th Circuit Court of Appeals in Atlanta.
None of those mentioned in the case was immediately available for comment.
